title: RL-Pipeline: Ingest cleanser and backpressure shim for structured logs
creator: Priya Sharma
description: Problem: multiple Redwood services emit heterogeneous logging payloads (freeform message, repeated JSON envelopes, long base64 fields, inconsistent correlation headers). High cardinality fields and noisy duplicate events are inflating Loki storage and increasing query latency. We need a small, deployable component that normalizes, trims, and deduplicates logs before they reach the indexing cluster, while preserving tracing correlation and providing backpressure signals to producers.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Ingest cleanser accepts structured JSON and common plaintext logs, normalizes into the canonical schema (timestamp, level, service, env, tenant_id, trace_id, span_id, message, attrs)
2) Dedupe: identical log bursts from the same (service, trace_id, message-fingerprint) within a 30s window are collapsed into a single event with a count field
3) Size limits: payloads over 16KB are truncated with a deterministic hash stored separately; base64/binary fields are removed unless explicitly allowed by service config
4) Correlation headers preserved: traceparent, tracestate, x-request-id mapped to trace_id/span_id when available
5) PII redaction rules applied (configurable), and an audit-mode for security review that records redaction decisions without dropping data
6) Backpressure shim exposes a 503/429 pattern and Prometheus metrics (ingest_queue_length, drop_count, processing_latency_p95) and producer SDKs will fall back to local buffering/drop policies
7) Output format compatible with Loki push API and an optional ES/ELK compatibility shim for customers on private deployments

8) End-to-end e2e test that replays historical sample traffic (including a high-dup burst) demonstrates >40% storage reduction for the burst and <120ms added median latency at 99th percentile under typical load
implementation_notes: Implement service as a Rust binary (small memory footprint) with async workers; optional sidecar mode and centralized aggregator mode
Use Kafka (existing topic observability.raw-logs) as the primary ingress; support HTTP push gateway for lightweight producers
Schema registry: JSON Schema v7 with versioning and per-service schema mappings stored in config service

Dedupe algorithm: fingerprint = sha256(canonicalized_message + service + tenant + truncated_timestamp) hashed to 64-bit; store in in-memory LRU with 30s TTL per key; fall back to probabilistic Bloom filter if memory constrained
Enrichment: lookup tenant metadata (quota tier, retention policy) from tenant service; attach retention_override field for downstream routing
PII redaction: configurable regex sets with optional NLP-based redaction flag (in audit mode only until security approves)
Batching: chunk output to Loki in batches with adaptive sizing to respect Loki push limits; prefer 256KB chunks or fewer than 5000 events per batch
Metrics & tracing: instrument with OpenTelemetry; trace spans propagated and a top-level span created for each incoming request for correlation into Console dashboards
Config: feature flags to toggle dedupe on a per-service basis and to enable ES shim in Private deployments
rollout_plan: 1) Deploy binary to dev cluster in sidecar mode for a small set of non-critical services
2) Run in parallel (no-write) mode for 48h to validate canonicalization and redaction differences against existing pipeline
3) Canary: enable write-through for 5% of traffic for 72h with dashboards monitored
4) Gradual increase to 25% then 100% with automated rollback if drop_count > 0.5% of events or processing_latency_p95 > 500ms
5) Post-rollout audit: run storage/ingest cost analysis and update runbook
test_plan: Unit tests for normalization rules, fingerprinting, and redaction logic
Integration tests using synthetic producers for JSON/plaintext/large binary fields
E2E replay test that mirrors last quarter's high-duplication incident and verifies dedupe and storage delta
Load test to confirm 99th percentile <120ms added latency at 2x expected peak throughput
Security review and a PEN test focusing on redaction bypass and schema-related injection attacks
